findings.text: The reviewed run's head suite-arm log (/home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261003T170849683435-fsa-wall-mask-limited-and-residual/scratch/head_other_tests.log) opens directly on pytest output and carries none of the header lines (revision, tree, command, module, cwd) that its base counterpart (base_other_tests.log) and head_render_test.log carry. A reader cannot tell from the file alone which revision, tree or command produced the 1-failed/36-passed line it holds, so the head arm is reconstructable only by re-running it. I re-ran it (1 failed, 36 passed, EXIT=1, same id) to substantiate it.

Inherited, not introduced here: the painter guard treats a draw_flux_contours call as wall-guarded whenever the wall slot is present - any keyword.arg == 'wall' (line 403) or len(node.args) > WALL_POSITION_INDEX (line 405) - without checking the value is not None. A call passing wall=None positionally or by keyword would be reported as guarded although no raster is blanked. Latent: no site in this batch passes None (all pass row['wall'], a district tuple, or a local unit array), so this is a false-negative class, not a present miss. The scanner is unchanged by this node.

justifications.durability: The rule is pinned by a falsifiable static control: I stripped the wall= keyword from one site and the scanner immediately flagged that call (zero_residual_check.py:593, EXIT=1), so the guard reddens when the mask is removed rather than merely passing. The scanner is wired to a real test file (tests/test_renderer_wall_scan.py), so it is exercised by a manual pytest run rather than by a one-off. Weaknesses: only one of the five drivers (limited_row_shadow_census.py, via test_limited_row_shadow_render.py) has a behavioural test that executes a changed function; the other four are covered only by the static scanner, which asserts the wall slot is present, not that the mask is correct. And the inherited painter guard (tests/renderer_wall_scan.py:403-406) still counts any wall keyword or a 9th positional argument as guarded without checking the value is non-None, so a wall=None call would read as guarded - latent, no such call in this corpus, and inherited from the predecessor scanner this node does not modify (finding 2).
justifications.evidence: Every headline was reproduced first-hand. Head scanner at the five head files: EXIT=0, no records (my run, module under test = the committed tests/renderer_wall_scan.py unchanged by this node). Base arm against git-show base copies: EXIT=1 with the same 15 sites as base_scan.log. Mask effect probed directly (vertices 360 -> 146). Head suite arms re-run by me: tests/test_limited_row_shadow_render.py 4 passed EXIT=0; -m 'not slow' tests/test_exact_clip_memory.py tests/test_null_generator_admission.py 1 failed 36 passed EXIT=1, failure id test_raster_label_parity_over_both_analytic_fields, identical to the node's base arm - so added_failure_count is 0. Deductions: the node's head suite-arm log (scratch/head_other_tests.log) opens on pytest output and carries no revision/tree/command/module/cwd header, where its base counterpart and head_render_test.log do (finding 1), and the reviewed manifest never emits a structured baseline_suite/after_suite block, only prose and log paths, so a reader must reconstruct the arms from the logs.
justifications.fit: Minimal and idiomatic: no new dependency, no new abstraction, no renamed public surface. The change reuses the existing wall semantics of draw_flux_contours and, for the one direct axis.contour, mirrors the same blanking in a file-local helper rather than widening a public API - the right call for a dotted round-off-floor grid line the plotting rules keep as a grid contour. The wall objects passed are exactly the ones each driver already draws with draw_wall, and the helper's meshgrid convention matches draw_flux_contours, so the mask lands on the same grid. Deduction: _masked_field duplicates the inside-wall blanking logic that draw_flux_contours already implements, so the two must be kept in step by hand; a shared blanking helper would remove that coupling, though it would widen the painter API.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The node's goal - route every unguarded scattered-field renderer call in this batch through the wall mask - is met and I reproduced it independently. The third-party scanner (unchanged by this run) run against the five head-revision drivers prints no records and exits 0, while the identical command against the five base-revision files exits 1 listing exactly the 15 sites the node names. The mask is not a no-op: a probe drawing the same finite raster with and without wall= turns 360 contour vertices into 146, so passing the wall demonstrably blanks the outside-wall region. The single direct axis.contour (limited_shadow_before_after.py:760) is handled by the file-local _masked_field helper, which reproduces the draw_flux_contours blanking (the scanner's BLANKED_PRODUCERS already lists _masked_field). Every argument passed as wall= resolves in scope (row["wall"], a tuple, or a local unit array) and none is None. Full marks withheld because the node's own report table of figure paths is asserted without a reproduction and, per the dispatch, no figure was regenerated - correct scope, but the visual result of the mask on each driver is unverified by construction.
justifications.scope_discipline: The reviewed range 68762d363..f8ea2245a touches exactly six paths - the five named benchmark drivers and the one landing fragment - all inside the node's granted write paths; no nova/ product source, no test file, no plan and no shared index is touched, so the gate (tests/renderer_wall_scan.py) is genuinely third-party. The single commit carries a conventional subject and a substantive body, no AI trailer, and no plan/stage/ticket label in the message, the paths or the symbols; the new helper is named _masked_field by its mechanism. No stray clone, branch or worktree; no figure was rewritten (consistent with the generic-plotting rule that a repaired figure is regenerated, not recaptioned, in a later wave).
